org_1: Midlands Precision Engineering Ltd — precision components manufacturer supplying automotive and aerospace sectors
org_2: 120 users across finance, procurement, production planning, warehouse, and sales
org_5: Legacy system (Sage 200) end of support. Business growing rapidly — acquired two smaller manufacturers in 2025 and needs a unified platform across all three sites.
data_1: Four legacy systems: Sage 200 (finance), bespoke MRP system (production planning), Excel-based warehouse management, and a separate CRM. All need to be decommissioned or integrated.
data_2: No formal data audit completed. Known issues: duplicate customer records across the three sites, inconsistent product codes between the acquired businesses, and 8 years of historical production data in a proprietary format.
data_3: Not standardised. Each of the three sites manages its own supplier and customer lists independently. Chart of accounts differs between sites.
data_4: 8 years of transactional data. Approximately 45,000 active product SKUs across three sites. 2,800 active customer accounts.
data_5: GDPR applies. Export control regulations apply to aerospace components — data sovereignty is a compliance requirement. All data must remain within UK jurisdiction.
proc_1: Finance processes documented to Level 2 at the main site. Acquired businesses have minimal process documentation. Production planning and warehouse processes largely undocumented across all sites.
proc_2: Significant variation between the three sites in every functional area. Production scheduling, quality control, and despatch processes are all handled differently.
proc_3: No gap analysis completed. Management aware this is needed but have not resourced it yet.
proc_4: Strong preference for standard D365 BC processes over customisation. CEO has mandated a clean implementation — no bespoke development.
proc_5: Finance, Procurement, Inventory Management, Production Planning (Basic), Warehouse Management, Sales Order Management, Quality Control
people_1: Group CFO is executive sponsor. Highly engaged — attended all vendor selection meetings. Has implemented ERP before at a previous company.
people_2: Group IT Manager identified as internal project lead. Will need external D365 BC implementation partner for the full programme. Super users identified at finance level only — not yet across other functions.
people_3: Main site migrated from a paper-based system to Sage 200 twelve years ago. Acquired businesses have never implemented a new ERP — both were running legacy systems from the 1990s.
people_4: No change management plan in place. HR Director aware it is needed. Warehouse and production staff have raised concerns about job security following the acquisitions.
people_5: Production and warehouse staff resistance is high — concerns about job security and distrust following acquisitions. Finance team broadly supportive. Sales team sceptical about CRM integration.
tech_1: Mix of on-premise servers at the main site and no formal IT infrastructure at the two acquired sites (they were running desktop applications). Moving to Microsoft Azure cloud with this implementation.
tech_2: Required integrations: production machinery data feeds (IoT sensors on CNC machines), customer EDI (top 5 automotive customers require EDI), payroll (ADP), and a quality management system (ISOTracker).
tech_3: Group IT Manager plus one IT support technician. Will need significant external support for Azure infrastructure, D365 implementation, and integrations. No internal D365 expertise.
tech_4: Export control compliance (ITAR and EAR) applies to aerospace components. Audit trail requirements are strict. Quality data must be retained for 10 years.
tech_5: No technical architecture review completed. Azure landing zone design not started.
gov_1: No formal project governance in place. Currently being managed as an IT project by the Group IT Manager. No steering committee formed.
gov_2: Budget approved in principle: £680,000 covering implementation partner, licences, infrastructure, training, data migration, and 15% contingency. Board has not formally signed off the detailed breakdown.
gov_4: 1. Data migration complexity — four legacy systems, three sites, inconsistent data. 2. Change resistance — especially at acquired businesses where trust is low post-acquisition. 3. Integration complexity — IoT, EDI, and quality system integrations are technically complex.
gov_5: No benefits realisation plan. CFO expects 30% reduction in month-end close time and elimination of manual Excel-based reporting within 12 months of go-live.
